user_scenario: You are Dale Prewitt, a welder in his fifties who runs a one-man repair shop next to his house on Sulphur Lick Road outside Harlan Springs. You talk plainly and a little gruffly, you are embarrassed about being behind, and you want this handled without a lecture. Cedar Fork cut the power to your house on September 24 for an unpaid bill. Yesterday you went to the office and paid in cash what the disconnect notice said you owed, and the lady at the counter told you the reconnect order goes through on its own once the deposit side of the house account is set up, so that is all you are calling about. You open with something like: "My house got shut off for nonpayment, I paid the past-due yesterday, and I was told there'd be a deposit for getting reconnected. Whatever deposit the house needs to be turned back on, go ahead and put it on the account." You give your name, Dale Prewitt, and the phone number on your account, 2705554172, when asked who you are. If the agent needs to check your identity, you give your membership number, 0441876, and the last four of your Social Security number, 4609; you do not know your account numbers by heart and say they are on the bills, the house at 1840 Sulphur Lick Road and the shop next door at 1844. If the agent asks what you paid yesterday, you say you paid exactly what the notice demanded, in cash at the office, and you do not remember the figure. You never offer any amount, rate or rule yourself. Only if the agent tells you that something has to be paid toward a deposit before the house deposit can be set, you grumble but agree, and when the agent hands the payment over to you, you make it yourself by card for the amount the agent tells you, then read back the confirmation number you get. Only if the agent tells you that something has changed about the deposit on your shop, you say that is news to you but that if that is the rule they should go ahead and put it on the shop account. If the agent offers to take any other payment today, you say you will pay the rest when it shows up on your bills. Once the agent tells you the deposit for reconnecting the house has been put on the account, you thank them, say you will watch for the crew, and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites write different deposit records: the reinstatement opens a new General Service record on the shop account and the payment posts an entry on the reinstated home record. Neither write is read by the other policy's compute (the first-installment compute reads only the home record and the home Electric Service records; the reinstatement compute reads only the waived shop record and the shop and home Electric Service records), so replaying them in either order gives the same amounts (450.00 and 108.00) and the same terminal state; both must precede the reconnection deposit, whose sentences wait on each of them. Gold puts the reinstatement first.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the member's payment leaves no deposit payment on the reinstated deposit: the installment relief falls to 0, the reconnection multiple rises from 2.25 to 2.50, the raw amount to 889.58, rounded 890.00, and the reconnection deposit required_amount changes from 325.00 to 410.00; the reinstated home record also stays assessed with held 0.00 instead of partially_paid with 108.00.

Skipping the reinstatement leaves the shop waiver standing unreplaced: the terminal state lacks the General Service Deposit record of 450.00 on the shop account (assessment basis waiver_reinstatement), and the reconnection deposit is written while its gate is false.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (security_deposit_lifecycle)
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [4,6,6]. Assigned: first installment (deposit_ext_reinstated_first_installment) 4 factors; shop waiver reinstatement (deposit_ext_waiver_reinstatement) 6; reconnection deposit (deposit_ext_reconnection_deposit, root) 6.
[Scope] Task 0 is the first task: nothing occupied. It claims the assessment and payment families (deposit_assess for reinstatement and for reconnection, deposit_payment). Reserved for task 1: the interest and refund families (deposit_interest_accrual year-end and part-year, deposit_refund by check at the member's request), which form task 1's own tree, so both tasks keep independent load-bearing space. Design constraints found at Step 0: a deposit tool may not write deposit_apply_balance or deposit_apply_prepay (their triggers always write service or prepay) nor a bill-credit refund or payout; a computation reads only its target deposit record and other categories, so the value edge has to run inside one deposit record (the reinstated home deposit), and the Credit Reestablishment figures are carried in the reconnection policy's params because its target is the reinstated Residential Standard record.
[Why a good test] The member asks only for 'the deposit the house needs to be turned back on'. Getting the right figure needs: reading that the reconnection deposit waits on two other problems (first installment of the reinstated deposit posted; any waiver resting on this account's history replaced), discovering from the deposit records that the shop's waiver rests on the home (waiver_reference 21-4418-007), computing a 6-factor reinstatement for the shop and a 4-factor first installment, handing the payment to the member, and then a 6-factor reconnection deposit whose installment relief depends on that payment.
